title: NY State Assembly · District 75
area: Manhattan's West Side, including Chelsea, Hell's Kitchen (Clinton), Hudson Yards, Midtown, Times Square, the Garment District and part of the Upper West Side/Lincoln Center area.

context.text: Incumbent Tony Simone defeated Emily YueXin Miller 76.5%-22.5% in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary. Miller had also sought the Conservative Party line but was withdrawn/disqualified from that primary and does not appear on the November ballot. Simone also holds the Working Families Party line. Christine Fontanelli (who also runs her campaign as "Cristina Fontanelli") advanced unopposed on the Republican line and also holds the "Save NYC Party" ballot line.

candidates.name: Tony Simone
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary 76.5%-22.5% over Emily YueXin Miller; also the Working Families Party nominee.

summary.text: Tony Simone is the Democratic and Working Families Party incumbent seeking re-election to a third term representing Manhattan's West Side, including Chelsea, Hell's Kitchen and Midtown. Before his 2022 election he worked in government and the nonprofit sector, including for state and city elected officials, People for the American Way and Friends of Hudson River Park. His official biography says he is focused on public safety, mental health, affordable housing, health care, climate change, tenant and immigrant rights, and equity for disabled people and LGBTQ+ New Yorkers.

background.text: Born in Queens, New York, in 1970. His mother was born in Peru and immigrated to New York City in 1968; his father, born in Astoria, drove taxis and trucks, and his late grandfather was a Teamsters union delegate.

Received a BA in political science and a BS in applied economics from Hofstra University (1994, per Ballotpedia) and an MPA from Columbia University's School of International and Public Affairs (2001, per Ballotpedia).
Began his government career working for the late state Sen. Catherine Abate and for then-City Councilmember Christine Quinn, and worked in the office of New York State Comptroller H. Carl McCall.
Served as deputy director of the northeast regional office of People for the American Way, where he led policy and field operations and organized on immigrant and LGBT rights.

Returned to government as Director of Community Outreach for the NYC Council under Speaker Christine Quinn, where his official biography says he directed volunteer relief efforts after Superstorm Sandy, led local initiatives to reduce hate crimes, advocated for marriage equality and worked to protect tenants.
Most recently before the Assembly, was Director of External Affairs at Hudson River Park Friends, working on fundraising and advocacy for the waterfront park.

Elected to the Assembly in 2022, defeating Republican Joseph A. Maffia with 84.7% of the vote in the November 8 general election, and took office January 1, 2023; re-elected in 2024 with 99.1% of the vote.

Current Assembly committee memberships are Corporations, Authorities and Commissions; Economic Development, Job Creation, Commerce and Industry; Election Law; Environmental Conservation; Governmental Operations; and Labor. He is also a member of the Black, Puerto Rican, Hispanic & Asian Legislative Caucus, the Task Force on New Americans and the Puerto Rican/Hispanic Task Force.
His official biography says he has been a campaign volunteer and staffer for decades, and that he lives in Hell's Kitchen with his husband, Jason, and their rescue dog.

priorities.text: Civil rights, racial and economic justice, including reproductive choice, LGBTQ+ equality and immigrant rights.
Housing: supports good-cause eviction, rent protections for market-rate housing, and tenant-protection bills, along with housing for homeless and low/middle-income residents.
Climate change: supports public renewable energy, improved mass transit, and all-electric buildings.
Public safety: released a plan addressing illegal guns from other states, community-police relations, the mental health crisis, and youth programs.

positions.summary: Supports good-cause eviction protections and rent protections for market-rate housing.
positions.quote: I support good cause eviction, rent protections for market rate housing, bills to protect tenants, & housing for people who are homeless, low- & middle- income w/o subsidizing developers.

positions.summary: Supports public renewable energy, improved mass transit and all-electric buildings.
positions.quote: NYS needs a radical green agenda. I support public renewable energy, improved mass transit, all electric buildings, and will work to improve water & air quality.

positions.summary: In a 2024 club questionnaire, described codifying Roe v. Wade and making New York a sanctuary for people seeking and providing abortions as critical steps.
positions.quote: Codifying Roe v Wade and ensuring we are a sanctuary for those seeking and providing abortions were critical moves.

positions.summary: In a 2024 club questionnaire, said he cosponsors the New York Health Act and supports a single-payer universal health care system.
positions.quote: Yes, I am a proud cosponsor of the New York Health Act.

positions.summary: In a 2024 club questionnaire, said New York should pass the New York for All Act, which bars use of state and local funds to aid immigration enforcement.
positions.quote: A5685, New York for All, to prohibit the use of state and local funds to aid immigration enforcement.

positions.summary: In a March 2025 press release, proposed amending the state-controlled Penn-area General Project Plan, which he says prohibits thousands of housing units, to allow new housing.
positions.quote: The amended GPP would immediately enable the construction of thousands of permanent, affordable housing units currently prohibited under the State’s plan

record.text: Assembly committee assignments for 2025-2026: Corporations, Authorities and Commissions; Economic Development, Job Creation, Commerce and Industry; Environmental Conservation; Governmental Operations; Labor; and Social Services.
Unveiled a bill to legalize year-round outdoor dining statewide, working with restaurant owners, business improvement districts and advocates.
With Council Member Erik Bottcher, proposed amending the state's General Project Plan for the Penn Station area to add affordable housing and green space to the neighborhood surrounding Penn Station.
With Assemblymember Alex Bores and State Senator Rachel May, called for transitioning New York's property tax structure to a Land Value Tax to address the housing affordability crisis.
Issued a public statement opposing the removal of a Gilbert Baker Rainbow Flag from the Stonewall National Monument.

candidates.name: Christine Fontanelli
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Republican primary unopposed; also holds the "Save NYC Party" ballot line.

summary.text: Christine (Cristina) Fontanelli is the Republican and Save NYC Party nominee challenging incumbent Tony Simone. She describes herself as a lifelong New Yorker and an award-winning opera singer, actress and television host, and is the founder of a nonprofit supporting young performers. Her campaign site lists public safety, education, housing, cost of living, health care, and arts and culture as her issues.

background.text: Describes herself as a lifelong New Yorker and an award-winning opera singer, actress and television host with a decades-long international career.
According to her campaign website, she has performed with major orchestras and at venues including Carnegie Hall and Lincoln Center.
Founded the Cristina Fontanelli Foundation, a nonprofit that, according to her campaign website, supports young performers and expands access to the arts.
Her campaign website says her great-grandfather, Rocco Maria Marasco, was a past Assemblyman. Ballotpedia lists her as the Republican and Save NYC Party candidate.

priorities.text: Public safety: supports policies to "restore law and order," hold repeat offenders accountable, and secure neighborhoods, subways and streets.
Cost of living: wants to reduce taxes, cut regulations and support small businesses.
Housing: wants to reduce regulations, encourage responsible development and expand housing supply.

positions.summary: Says she will work to reduce burdensome regulations, encourage responsible development, and promote solutions that expand housing supply.
positions.quote: I will work to reduce burdensome regulations, encourage responsible development, and promote solutions that expand housing supply.

statements.quote: Healthcare should be accessible and affordable for all New Yorkers. I support policies that increase competition, access to care, and reduce costs while ensuring patients and doctors, not government bureaucrats, are making healthcare decisions.

No official record exists for her since she has not held office. Her biography is limited to her campaign website; no news profile or Ballotpedia survey was found.
